questions.q: According to the summary, what happens when you stop forcing focus and let your mind rest?
a: You can produce up to 40% more original ideas
You permanently lose the thread of the task
You become more anxious about unfinished work
You need much longer to return to deep focus
questions.why: The first lesson cites studies showing rest and open awareness generate up to 40% more original ideas.

questions.q: What does Goleman say is a surprisingly powerful way to build willpower?
a: Doing work you genuinely love
Getting more sleep every night
Taking a short break every hour
Rewarding yourself after each task
questions.why: The second lesson argues willpower is mostly psychological, and work that reflects your goals becomes effortless.

questions.q: Why did George Lucas break away from his production company while making Star Wars?
a: He feared his creative vision would be compromised
He wanted a larger effects budget
He disagreed with the film's lead actor
He was offered a better deal elsewhere
questions.why: The summary uses Lucas, who went rogue because he believed in his idea, as an example of love-powered willpower.

questions.q: How does Goleman suggest we make better decisions about the distant future?
a: Treat far-off problems as immediate threats
Set a firm deadline for every small task
Focus only on what can be finished this year
Ask others to hold us accountable weekly
questions.why: The third lesson says imagining long-term consequences as happening tomorrow helps us stop choosing short-term comfort.

questions.q: What does the summary call the hidden driver of excellence?
a: Attention
Discipline
Talent
Luck
questions.why: The overview describes Goleman's book as being about attention, which he calls the hidden driver of excellence.
